## Deliverables

### D1: Sprint Backlog (GitHub Issues)

The team selects and prepares the issues it will implement in Sprint 1.

> **Start this early.** Issues may turn out to be broader than expected, overlap with each other, or be invalid. Discovering this in week 2 leaves no time to recover.

**Step 1: Refine the backlog.** Go through all open issues as a team. Add missing ones, close invalid or duplicate ones, and decompose any large or XL issues into smaller sub-issues that can be completed within the sprint. Record decisions in a team meeting (preferred) or Zulip thread.

**Step 2: Estimate and select.** Use the prioritization and estimation techniques from the planning lecture (story points and planning poker) to size and rank your backlog. ### D7: Sprint Release

At the end of Sprint 1, create a release tag to mark the sprint's end state.

- Ensure all Sprint 1 PRs are merged before tagging.
- Use the same base version from Sprint 0 (no version bump).
- Tag with the `-csci435-s1` suffix. Example: if Sprint 0 was `v2.17.2-csci435-s0`, tag Sprint 1 as `v2.17.2-csci435-s1`.
- Write a release description listing features added, bugs fixed, or improvements made this sprint.

```bash
git tag v<version>-csci435-s1
git push origin v<version>-csci435-s1
```

Create the GitHub release from the tag on the repository's Releases page.

**Submission:** Link to the GitHub release in D6. Tag pushed by Oct 8, 11:59 PM.

### D4 PR grading detail

All PRs associated with each issue are graded on the criteria below. The D4 score is the aggregate across all issues, normalized to 36 points.

| Criterion | Points per PR |
|---|---|
| Change correctly implements the acceptance criteria from D2 | 6 |
| Tests written or updated appropriately; test strategy explained in PR | 5 |
| PR description clearly explains what changed, why, and how it was tested | 4 |
| CI passes (or manual verification documented) | 3 |
| Code reviewed using the rubric; reviewer comment posted on PR | 2 |
| **Total per PR** | **20** |

> **Minimum bar.** A team with no merged PRs (D4), no sprint report (D6), or no release (D7) receives a **0 for Sprint 1** regardless of other deliverables.

> **Extra credit.** A PR submitted to the real upstream project and accepted or under active review earns up to **3 bonus points per PR**, at the instructor's discretion.

# Medusa / CSCI 535 — Context Handoff

Written 2026-09-28, at the end of the Sprint 0 chat. Point a new session at this file first.

## 1. Who and what

- **Me:** Alex Grapsas, GitHub `angrapsas`, email angrapsas@wm.edu
- **Course:** CSCI 435/535 Software Engineering. Team **Perseus**.
- **Repo:** https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/medusa (shared team repo, everyone has write access)
- **Upstream:** Medusa v2.17.2, an open source commerce platform
- **Default branch:** `develop`. **There is no `main`.** Several course docs say `main`; ignore that, every PR targets `develop`.

**Team GitHub handles:** `angrapsas` (me), `lefecko` (Logan Fecko), `njpiombino` (Nicholas Piombino),
`maali-ux`, `gracieagomes`. Instructor/TA is `musta55` (repo admin).

Branch-based workflow, not forks. Prefixes: `feat/issue-<N>-...`, `fix/issue-<N>-...`, `chore/...`.

---

## 2. How to run it

Everything is already installed and configured. Node is managed by nvm.

```bash
# interactive terminals pick this up from ~/.zshrc automatically.
# a non-interactive shell (like an agent's Bash tool) does NOT, so prefix with:
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"; . /opt/homebrew/opt/nvm/nvm.sh; nvm use 22
export COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0
```

Toolchain: Node 22.23.2 (nvm), Yarn 3.2.1 (via corepack), Docker 28.4.0, gh 2.100.0 (authed as angrapsas).
Do NOT use Node 24 — some suites fail on it. Homebrew also has a Node 26 that nvm shadows.

### Two separate apps

**A. The monorepo** at `~/medusa` — the actual Medusa source, what we make PRs against.

```bash
cd ~/medusa
yarn install                                    # ~1 min
yarn build                                      # ~2.5 min, 80 packages
yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard dev          # admin dashboard dev server on :5173
yarn workspace @medusajs/ui storybook           # design system on :6006
```

**B. A scaffolded store** at `~/my-store` — created with create-medusa-app, used to click around a
real running store. Uses PUBLISHED medusa packages from npm, NOT the local source, so changes to
`~/medusa` do NOT show up here.

```bash
docker start medusa-postgres                    # postgres:15 on :5433, db `my_store`, postgres/postgres
cd ~/my-store/apps/backend && npm run dev       # admin at :9000/app
```

Admin login exists (created during Sprint 0). Store is seeded: 4 products, 20 variants, 2 orders,
1 region (Europe/EUR), 1 sales channel.

**Which one to use:** :5173 to see your own dashboard changes. :9000 to see a fully working store
with data. They are different codebases.

### Tests

```bash
cd ~/medusa
yarn workspace @medusajs/medusa test            # Jest, backend, 13 suites / 95 tests
yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard test         # Vitest, frontend, ~13 files / 93 tests
yarn turbo run test --no-daemon --no-cache --force --continue   # everything; KEEP --continue
```

Frameworks: **Jest 29** (backend), **Vitest 3** + @testing-library/react + jsdom (frontend).
No Playwright, no Cypress, no browser automation anywhere. ~1050 `.spec.ts(x)` files.

Integration tests need their own containers and will take the my-store DB offline:

```bash
docker stop medusa-postgres
docker run -d --name medusa-pg -e POSTGRES_USER=postgres -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -p 5433:5432 postgres:16-alpine
docker run -d --name medusa-redis -p 6380:6379 redis:7-alpine
cd ~/medusa && DB_HOST=localhost DB_PORT=5433 DB_USERNAME=postgres DB_PASSWORD=postgres \
  yarn workspace @medusajs/region test:integration      # 18/18
# teardown
docker rm -f medusa-pg medusa-redis && docker start medusa-postgres
```

## 3. Known broken things (all upstream Medusa, not our fork)

Our fork only adds STUDENTS.md and course files on top of Medusa 2.17.2. These are real upstream bugs.

**1. 467 unit tests fail on a clean checkout.** `@medusajs/icons` 464/464 and `@medusajs/ui` 3/40.
All from one cause: `packages/design-system/icons/package.json` declares
`react: "^18.3.1 || ^19.0.0"` in devDependencies, so Yarn nests react@19.2.6 inside that package
while `react-dom@18.3.1` stays hoisted at root. React 19 elements + React 18 renderer =
"Objects are not valid as a React child". Fix: scoped resolution `"@medusajs/icons/react": "^18.3.1"`
in root package.json — precedent already exists there for `@redocly/cli/react`.
**68 of 70 packages pass.** Confirmed by three of us independently. NOT your machine.

**2. The standalone dashboard dev server renders a blank page.**
`packages/admin/dashboard/vite.config.mts` defines only 3 of the 6 globals the source needs.
Missing: `__AUTH_TYPE__`, `__JWT_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY__`, `__MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE__`.
`src/lib/client/client.ts:3` throws a ReferenceError before React mounts. The bundled admin at
:9000 works because `admin-bundler/src/utils/config.ts:52-57` defines all six. Config was last
touched 2024-10-09; the source added those globals in late 2025. Nobody has fixed it.
Workaround already in the repo: `vi.hoisted()` in three spec files sets the globals for tests.

**3. Form validation errors never display anywhere in the dashboard.**
`@hookform/resolvers@3.4.2` with `zod@4.2.0`. Resolvers v3 doesn't understand zod 4 errors, so
instead of putting them in form state it throws. **116 files use zodResolver, 104 render
`<Form.ErrorMessage />`, and none of them can show anything.** Submitting an invalid form just
silently refuses. Verified by running validation directly: errors exist with messages, they just
never reach the form.

## 6. My two big issues, explained

**#16 — Retain failed and reverted workflow executions.**
Medusa runs business logic as *workflows*: multi-step operations where each step can declare a
compensation function that undoes it if a later step fails (saga pattern). The admin has a page at
`/app/settings/workflows` with a timeline that colors failed steps red and shows what compensated.
It is empty on every install. Executions are only kept if the workflow sets `retentionTime`, and
**1 of 339 workflows does** (`complete-cart.ts:340`, three days). `finishedStates` includes DONE,
FAILED and REVERTED, so failures get deleted like successes —
`workflow-engine-inmemory/src/utils/workflow-orchestrator-storage.ts:415` and the same logic in
`workflow-engine-redis/.../workflow-orchestrator-storage.ts:631`. Proposal: keep FAILED/REVERTED by
default, configurable window, add pruning. The objection to answer is storage cost; keeping only
failures scales with failure rate, not traffic.

**#23 — Workflow lifecycle controls.**
The engine implements `retryStep`, `cancel` and `resume`. The admin API has 8 workflow routes
(list, view, subscribe x2, run, steps/success, steps/failure) and exposes **none** of those three.
So you can start a workflow and watch it, but can't act on one that's stuck or failed. Must be core
— a plugin can't add routes under `packages/medusa/src/api/admin`. Depends on #16.

These two are related but distinct: #16 is a storage policy in the engines, #23 is new API routes
plus UI. Near-zero file overlap.

**Two engines:** `workflow-engine-inmemory` (default, state in process memory) and
`workflow-engine-redis` (adds `ioredis` + `bullmq` for scheduled retries and timeouts, survives
restarts, works across multiple servers). Any engine change must touch both.

---

## 7. Lesson learned about proposing features

Medusa core is deliberately minimal; the plugin ecosystem fills feature gaps. **Before proposing
anything, search externally, not just the repo.** Ideas that looked like gaps but already exist as
official or community plugins: Shopify migration (Medusa's own MCP server does it), sales analytics
dashboard (Agilo and rsc-labs plugins), abandoned cart recovery (community plugin + Medusa guide).

The proposals that survive are ones a plugin **cannot** add — engine behavior, admin API routes,
core defaults. That's why #16 and #23 hold up.

Also verified as genuinely missing: order CSV import (products have import+export, orders have
export only), customer export, and **a count of how many times a product has sold** —
`order_line_item` has indexed `product_id` and `variant_id` plus `quantity`, so the data is there
and indexed; nobody surfaced it. That last one is a natural sequel to #9 (order count + lifetime
spend for customers, which lefecko already merged).

## 9. Conventions to follow

- Prettier: no semicolons, double quotes, 2-space indent, ES5 trailing commas. `npx prettier --check <files>`
- Files kebab-case, types PascalCase, functions camelCase, constants SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, DB fields snake_case
- Commit style is mixed on the team: conventional (`feat(dashboard): ...`) and plain imperative both appear
- **Changesets required** — add one as a separate `chore:` commit. See `.changeset/` for format
- PR description format: What / Why / How / Testing, in plain prose, first person. Include the
  command to run the tests. No checklists, no bolded headers — teammates don't use them
- `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` trailers appear on some commits (lefecko uses them, upstream Medusa
  does too). Not required
- AI logs go to `ai-logs/sprint0/<username>/YYYY-MM-DD_claude-code_<desc>.md` from `~/.specstory/history/`

## 10. How I like to work

- Find the code myself first, then use AI to check my understanding. The course grades this
  ("concept location") and I have to be able to explain every line of my own PRs
- Verify claims by running things, don't assert from reading. Prove a test fails without the fix
- Don't post to GitHub (issues, PRs, comments, reviews, tags) without showing me the exact text first
- Keep writing plain. No em dashes, no AI-sounding scaffolding. Match my teammates' register

### D2: Requirements Specification

For each issue in your Sprint 1 backlog, the owner must write or significantly refine the specification **before writing any code**.

**Format:** If your project already uses an issue template, adapt it to include the fields below. If your project has no feature request template, create one. Otherwise, use the following structure as a guide.

For **features and enhancements**, write the issue as a user story that satisfies the INVEST criteria (see also the slides on Project management):

```markdown
## User Story
As a [type of user], I want [goal] so that [benefit].

## User Scenario
[A concrete walkthrough of how a user encounters and uses this feature.]

## Acceptance Criteria
1. ...
2. ...
3. ...

## Out of Scope
- ...

## Open Questions
- ...
```

Each acceptance criterion must be **testable**: observable behavior, not vague intent. **Minimum 3 per issue.**

> **What makes a criterion testable?** A testable criterion has a clear pass/fail outcome. "The export button is disabled when no items are selected" is testable. "The UI should feel responsive" is not. If you cannot write a test or manual step that definitively passes or fails it, rewrite it.

For **bug reports**, include at minimum:

```markdown
## Observed Behavior (OB)
[What currently happens.]

## Expected Behavior (EB)
[What should happen instead.]

## Steps to Reproduce (S2R)
1. ...
2. ...

## Additional Information
[Screenshots, stack traces, error logs — recommended.]
```

**Before finalizing your spec,** have at least one teammate read it and leave a comment on the issue confirming it is clear enough to implement. This is a lightweight requirements review.

**Submission:** All issue specs updated in GitHub. Links included in D6.

---

### D3: Design Decisions

For each issue in your Sprint 1 backlog, the owner must document **at least one non-trivial design decision** before or during implementation.

**What to document:**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Decision | One sentence stating what you decided |
| Alternatives considered | At least two concrete options you evaluated |
| Rationale | Why you chose this option over the others |
| Consequences | What this decision makes easier and what it makes harder |

**Where to put it:** Add a `## Design` section to the GitHub issue body, in an issue comment, or include it in the PR description. For decisions that affect multiple issues or the overall architecture, add a team-level note to `docs/sprint1/design.md`.

> **Don't overthink the scope.** "Should I add this field to the existing component or create a new one?" with a clear rationale is a perfectly good design decision. The goal is to make your reasoning visible; one sentence per field is enough. This is not a design document.

**Submission:** Design decisions documented in GitHub issues, PR descriptions, or `docs/sprint1/design.md`. Links in D6.

=================== #11
Add import inventory from csv file
## User Story
As a store manager, I want to upload a CSV file to import multiple inventory items at once so that I can migrate inventory data without manually entering each one individually.

## User Scenario
A user is migrating their store to Medusa from another platform and has 300 existing inventory items to recreate. They export their inventory from the old platform, reformat the data to match Medusa's CSV template, and upload the file from the Inventory list page. Medusa validates the file and surfaces a clear error message identifying four rows with duplicate SKUs. They fix the CSV and re-upload. All 300 inventory items are created successfully and appear in the Inventory list.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. An "Import Inventory" action is available on the Inventory list page, consistent in placement and interaction pattern with the existing product CSV import.
2. A downloadable CSV template is provided covering all fields available when creating an inventory item:
    - Required: Title, SKU, Requires Shipping, In Stock, Location
    - Optional: Description, Width, Length, Height, Weight, MID Code, HS Code, Country of Origin, Material
3. The uploaded CSV is validated before any inventory items are created; if any row is invalid the entire import is rejected and no items are created.
4. Validation feedback identifies each failing row by row number and describes the specific error (e.g. missing required field, duplicate SKU within the file, SKU already exists in Medusa, invalid value for Requires Shipping).
5. On successful import, all inventory items in the CSV are created in a single operation and immediately appear in the Inventory list assigned to the European Warehouse location.
6. The import UI follows the same component patterns as the existing product CSV import.
7. Required fields that are empty/blank throw an error; optional fields that are blank are accepted.

## Out of Scope
- Updating or deduplicating inventory items that already exist in Medusa (all imports should be new inventory items).
- Scheduling or deferring import jobs. The operation completes synchronously within the request.
- Exporting existing inventory to CSV.

## Open Questions
- Is there a maximum file size or row count limit that should be enforced?
- Should "In Stock" quantities below zero be rejected as invalid, or are negative values permitted?
- Can there be multiple locations?
=================== #40
Add import customers from csv file
## User Story
As a store manager, I want to upload a CSV file to import multiple customers at once so that I can migrate customer data without manually entering each one individually.

## User Scenario
A user is migrating their store to Medusa from another platform and has 500 existing customers to recreate. They export their customers from the old platform, reformat the data to match Medusa's CSV template, and upload the file from the Customer list page. Medusa validates the file and surfaces a clear error message identifying two rows with duplicate email addresses. They fix the CSV and re-upload. All 500 customers are created successfully and appear in the Customer list.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. An "Import Customers" action is available on the Customer list page, consistent in placement and interaction pattern with the existing product CSV import.
2. A downloadable CSV template is provided, covering all fields available when creating a customer: email (required), first name, last name, company, and phone (all optional).
3. The uploaded CSV is validated before any customers are created; if any row is invalid the entire import is rejected and no customers are created.
4. Validation feedback identifies each failing row by row number and describes the specific error (e.g. missing email, invalid email format, duplicate email within the file, email already exists in Medusa).
5. On successful import, all customers in the CSV are created in a single operation and immediately appear in the Customer list.
6. The import UI follows the same component patterns as the existing product CSV import.
7. Required fields that are empty/blank throw an error; optional fields that are blank are accepted.

## Out of Scope
- Customer group assignment. This is not part of the create customer fields and is out of scope for this story.
- Updating or deduplicating customers that already exist in Medusa (all imports should be new customers).
- Scheduling or deferring import jobs. The operation completes synchronously within the request.
- Exporting existing customers to CSV.

## Open Questions
- Is there a maximum file size or row count limit that should be enforced?

import {
  MedusaResponse,
  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
} from "@medusajs/framework/http"
import type { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import type { AdminImportProductsType } from "../validators"
import { importProductsAsChunksWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"

/**
 * @since 2.8.5
 */
export const POST = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<AdminImportProductsType>,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminImportProductResponse>
) => {

    },

import {
  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
  MedusaResponse,
} from "@medusajs/framework/http"

import {
  importProductsAsChunksWorkflowId,
  waitConfirmationProductImportStepId,
} from "@medusajs/core-flows"
import { IWorkflowEngineService } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { Modules, TransactionHandlerType } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { StepResponse } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"

/**
 * @since 2.8.5
 */
export const POST = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
  res: MedusaResponse
) => {
  const workflowEngineService: IWorkflowEngineService = req.scope.resolve(
    Modules.WORKFLOW_ENGINE
  )
  const transactionId = req.params.transaction_id

  await workflowEngineService.setStepSuccess({
    idempotencyKey: {
      action: TransactionHandlerType.INVOKE,
      transactionId,
      stepId: waitConfirmationProductImportStepId,
      workflowId: importProductsAsChunksWorkflowId,
    },
    stepResponse: new StepResponse(true),
  })

  res.status(202).json({})
}

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**#32 (customer count on groups) already exists upstream. What should happen to it?**

Options:
- **Swap for another small issue** - Comment on #32 showing the existing column, close it, and pick a different small issue written by a teammate.
- **Reframe it** - Keep #32 but change it to something not yet built, e.g. sorting groups by size. The current column can't be sorted, and it loads every customer ID just to count them. This would need a backend change.
- **Draft both, decide later** - I write the closing comment and a reframed spec; you pick after talking to maali-ux.

**For the CSV imports (#11, #40), which flow should the specs describe?**

Options:
- **Match product import (Recommended)** - Upload, see a summary, confirm, then the import runs in the background with a notification. Consistent with the existing import and reuses its UI. Remove the 'synchronous' out-of-scope line.
- **Synchronous** - One request that checks and creates everything, then returns. Simpler to build and test, but it doesn't match product import, so drop the 'consistent with product import' criteria.

**For #11, how should the CSV specify stock location?**

Options:
- **Location column by name (Recommended)** - Optional 'Location' and 'Stocked Quantity' columns. Names must match an existing stock location, otherwise that row fails. One location per row.
- **Pick location in the UI** - The user chooses one stock location in the import modal, and every row gets stock there. No location column.
- **No stock levels** - Import only creates the inventory items. Stock is set afterwards. Simplest.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 02:04:50Z)**_

You're right about the first part. The second part doesn't hold, because the count is already on screen.

**The fields string** (line 48):
```
id,name,created_at,updated_at,customers.id
```
So yes, each group comes back with its list of customers, with only each customer's `id` filled in.

**The columns in `useColumns`** (lines 133-198):
1. `name` (sortable)
2. `customers`, with the header `t("customers.domain")`, which renders as "Customers"
3. `created_at` (sortable)
4. `updated_at` (sortable)
5. the actions menu (Edit, Delete)

**The data is already displayed.** Column 2 at lines 140-145 is the customer count:
```tsx
cell: ({ row }) => {
  return <span>{row.original.customers?.length ?? 0}</span>
},
```
It takes the `customers` list that came back from the API and shows how many items it has. That's the exact feature #32 asks for. It came from upstream in commit `fcd3e2226e` (Feb 2025, "Migrate SC tables to DataTable").

So as #32 is written, nothing is missing. The column does have two real limits, if you want to reframe the issue rather than drop it:
- **It can't be sorted.** It has no `enableSorting`, unlike name and the dates. Sorting by group size would need a backend change, because the count is worked out in the browser, not stored or calculated by the API.
- **It pays for the count by fetching every member's ID.** A group with 10,000 customers sends back 10,000 IDs just to show one number.

If you want to see it for yourself, the customer groups page on the store at :9000 runs the same upstream code. Any group with members should already show a Customers column.

import { PencilSquare, Trash } from "@medusajs/icons"
import { Button, Container, Heading, toast, usePrompt } from "@medusajs/ui"
import { keepPreviousData } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { createColumnHelper } from "@tanstack/react-table"
import { useMemo } from "react"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
import { Link } from "react-router-dom"

import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"
import {
  Action,
  ActionMenu,
} from "../../../../../components/common/action-menu"
import { PermissionGuard } from "../../../../../components/common/permission-guard"
import { _DataTable } from "../../../../../components/table/data-table"
import {
  useCustomers,
  useDeleteCustomer,
} from "../../../../../hooks/api/customers"
import { useCustomerTableColumns } from "../../../../../hooks/table/columns/use-customer-table-columns"
import { useCustomerTableFilters } from "../../../../../hooks/table/filters/use-customer-table-filters"
import { useCustomerTableQuery } from "../../../../../hooks/table/query/use-customer-table-query"
import { useDataTable } from "../../../../../hooks/use-data-table"
import { usePermissions } from "../../../../../providers/permissions-provider"

const PAGE_SIZE = 20

export const CustomerListTable = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()

  const { searchParams, raw } = useCustomerTableQuery({ pageSize: PAGE_SIZE })
  const { customers, count, isLoading, isError, error } = useCustomers(
    {
      ...searchParams,
    },
    {
      placeholderData: keepPreviousData,
    }
  )

  const filters = useCustomerTableFilters()
  const columns = useColumns()

  const { table } = useDataTable({
    data: customers ?? [],
    columns,
    count,
    enablePagination: true,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    pageSize: PAGE_SIZE,
  })

  if (isError) {
    throw error
  }

  return (
    <Container className="divide-y p-0">
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between px-6 py-4">
        <Heading>{t("customers.domain")}</Heading>
        <PermissionGuard resource="customer" operation="create">
          <Link to="/customers/create">
            <Button size="small" variant="secondary">
              {t("actions.create")}
            </Button>
          </Link>
        </PermissionGuard>
      </div>
      <_DataTable
        table={table}
        columns={columns}
        pageSize={PAGE_SIZE}
        count={count}
        filters={filters}
        orderBy={[
          { key: "email", label: t("fields.email") },
          { key: "first_name", label: t("fields.firstName") },
          { key: "last_name", label: t("fields.lastName") },
          { key: "has_account", label: t("customers.hasAccount") },
          { key: "created_at", label: t("fields.createdAt") },
          { key: "updated_at", label: t("fields.updatedAt") },
        ]}
        isLoading={isLoading}
        navigateTo={(row) => row.original.id}
        search
        queryObject={raw}
        noRecords={{
          message: t("customers.list.noRecordsMessage"),
        }}
      />
    </Container>
  )
}

export const CustomerActions = ({
  customer,
}: {
  customer: HttpTypes.AdminCustomer
}) => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()
  const { can } = usePermissions()
  const prompt = usePrompt()

  const { mutateAsync } = useDeleteCustomer(customer.id)

  const handleDelete = async () => {
    const res = await prompt({
      title: t("customers.delete.title"),
      description: t("customers.delete.description", {
        email: customer.email,
      }),
      verificationInstruction: t("general.typeToConfirm"),
      verificationText: customer.email,
      confirmText: t("actions.delete"),
      cancelText: t("actions.cancel"),
    })

    if (!res) {
      return
    }

    await mutateAsync(undefined, {
      onSuccess: () => {
        toast.success(
          t("customers.delete.successToast", {
            email: customer.email,
          })
        )
      },
      onError: (error) => {
        toast.error(error.message)
      },
    })
  }

  const actions: Action[] = []

  if (can("customer", "update")) {
    actions.push({
      icon: <PencilSquare />,
      label: t("actions.edit"),
      to: `/customers/${customer.id}/edit`,
    })
  }

  if (can("customer", "delete")) {
    actions.push({
      icon: <Trash />,
      label: t("actions.delete"),
      onClick: handleDelete,
    })
  }

  if (!actions.length) {
    return null
  }

  return (
    <ActionMenu
      groups={[
        {
          actions,
        },
      ]}
    />
  )
}

const columnHelper = createColumnHelper<HttpTypes.AdminCustomer>()

const useColumns = () => {
  const columns = useCustomerTableColumns()

  return useMemo(
    () => [
      ...columns,
      columnHelper.display({
        id: "actions",
        cell: ({ row }) => <CustomerActions customer={row.original} />,
      }),
    ],
    [columns]
  )
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 02:26:14Z)**_

Yes, it's a real gap, and it looks small: it only needs dashboard changes, no backend work. Your reading of both files is right. I only read code for this and haven't checked it against the running store.

**1. The customer list has no groups column.** `use-customer-table-columns.tsx` defines four columns:
- `email`
- `name` (built from first and last name)
- `has_account`
- `created_at` ("First seen")

`customer-list-table.tsx` adds only an actions column on top of those. You can filter by group (`use-customer-table-filters.tsx:25`), and the filter value goes into the `groups` query param (`use-customer-table-query.tsx:32`). But the list request doesn't ask for `fields` at all, so it gets the default set, and groups aren't in it.

**2. The API already returns groups, so no backend work.**
- `groups` is in the `allowed` list in `packages/medusa/src/api/admin/customers/query-config.ts`. It just isn't in `defaultAdminCustomerFields`.
- The list endpoint already uses this today: `add-customers-form.tsx:69` calls `useCustomers({ fields: "id,email,first_name,last_name,has_account,*groups", ... })`.
- Integration tests also hit `?fields=*groups` (`integration-tests/http/__tests__/customer/admin/customer.spec.ts:326`).
- The `AdminCustomer` type already has `groups?: AdminCustomerGroup[]`.

So the change would be adding `*groups` (or `+groups.name`) to the fields in the list request, plus one new column.

**3. Nothing else shows groups per customer in a list.**
- **Customer detail page** (`customer-group-section.tsx`): shows the groups for one customer. It's a single-customer view, not a list.
- **Add customers to group form**: fetches `*groups`, but only uses them at line 94 to disable customers who are already in the group. It never displays them.
- **Customers table on the group detail page**: uses the same shared columns, so it has no groups column either. That table already sits inside one group, so a groups column matters less there.

**4. The "-" vs 0 difference is real, and you read it correctly.**
- `customer-group-general-section.tsx` renders `group.customers?.length || "-"`. Zero counts as false for `||`, so an empty group shows "-".
- The groups list uses `?? 0` (`customer-group-list-table.tsx:143`), which only replaces null or undefined, so the same group shows 0 there.
- Both pages fetch `customers.id` (the detail page uses `CUSTOMER_GROUP_DETAIL_FIELDS = "+customers.id"`), so the data is identical. Only the operator differs.

This is a one-character fix, so it's probably a better fit as a note inside the new issue than as an issue of its own.

**Things the spec should decide so it stays small:**
- **Where the column goes.** `useCustomerTableColumns` is shared by three tables: the customer list, the customers table on the group detail page, and the add customers form. Adding the column there puts it in all three. Adding it only in `customer-list-table.tsx`'s local `useColumns` keeps it to the customer list. That choice could be your D3 design decision.
- **Customers in many groups.** For example, show the first one or two group names and then "+N".
- **Customers in no groups.** What the cell shows. This is the same "-" vs 0 question again, so pick one and match the rest of the dashboard.

One last check before you ask maali to rewrite #32: search the upstream medusajs/medusa repo for an open issue or PR about a groups column on the customer list. That's the mistake that bit you with #32.

Add Business Analytics to Medusa Admin Dashboard Home Page
njpiombino
type: feature,scope: medium
## User Story
As a store manager, I want to see a sales analytics overview on the dashboard home page so that I can assess business performance at a glance without navigating to multiple sections.

## User Scenario
A user who manages a mid-sized online store starts their day by logging into the Medusa admin dashboard. Instead of clicking through Orders and Products, they see a summary panel on the home page showing total revenue and their top 3 selling products.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The dashboard home page displays a summary panel showing: total revenue, total order count, and top-selling products (by units sold).
2. Revenue figures use the store's configured currency and formatting.
3. Top products show at least the product name and units sold; the list displays 3 entries.
4. All metrics reflect completed/paid orders only (not draft or cancelled).
5. If no orders exist, each metric displays a zero state with a brief empty-state message rather than an error or blank space.

## Out of Scope
- Real-time / live order stream updates (static snapshot on load is sufficient).
- Comparison to prior periods (e.g. "↑ 12% vs last week")
- Inventory, customer, or marketing metrics.
- CSV/PDF export of the summary data.
- Role-based visibility restrictions (all admin users see the panel).
- Time interval for data

## Open Questions
- What is the acceptable data freshness — real-time, or is a cache with a short TTL (e.g. 5 minutes) acceptable?
- Should the panel be dismissible or reorderable by the merchant, or is its position on the home page fixed?

import { Tooltip } from "@medusajs/ui"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"

import { SalesChannelDTO } from "@medusajs/types"
import { PlaceholderCell } from "../../common/placeholder-cell"

type SalesChannelsCellProps = {
  salesChannels?: SalesChannelDTO[] | null
}

export const SalesChannelsCell = ({
  salesChannels,
}: SalesChannelsCellProps) => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()

  // Filter out null/undefined entries that can occur when a sales channel
  // is deleted but the product association is not cleaned up
  const validChannels = salesChannels?.filter(
    (sc): sc is SalesChannelDTO => sc != null
  )

  if (!validChannels || !validChannels.length) {
    return <PlaceholderCell />
  }

  if (validChannels.length > 2) {
    return (
      <div className="flex h-full w-full items-center gap-x-1 overflow-hidden">
        <span className="truncate">
          {validChannels
            .slice(0, 2)
            .map((sc) => sc.name)
            .join(", ")}
        </span>
        <Tooltip
          content={
            <ul>
              {validChannels.slice(2).map((sc) => (
                <li key={sc.id}>{sc.name}</li>
              ))}
            </ul>
          }
        >
          <span className="text-xs">
            {t("general.plusCountMore", {
              count: validChannels.length - 2,
            })}
          </span>
        </Tooltip>
      </div>
    )
  }

  const channels = validChannels.map((sc) => sc.name).join(", ")

  return (
    <div className="flex h-full w-full max-w-[250px] items-center overflow-hidden">
      <span title={channels} className="truncate">
        {channels}
      </span>
    </div>
  )
}

export const SalesChannelHeader = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()

  return (
    <div className="flex h-full w-full items-center">
      <span>{t("fields.salesChannels")}</span>
    </div>
  )
}

I've finished the upstream search and have everything needed for the draft.

**Upstream search: nothing duplicates this**
- I searched upstream issues and PRs (open and closed) for "customer groups column", "customer list groups", "groups column customers", "display customer groups", and the two file names. None asks for a groups column on the customer list.
- **Two related open items:** issue #16872 ("Filtering Customers by Group Returns Undesired Customers") and its fix, PR #16881, which adds `$nin`/`$ne` operators to the groups filter. They change the API's filter validation, not the table columns, so they don't overlap. They're good to cite in Out of Scope.
- **Configurable tables:** upstream has a feature that lets users choose which columns a list shows. In this repo only products and orders use it, not customers, so it doesn't already give you a groups column.

**Folding in the "-" vs 0 fix**
- **Small:** not hurt. It's one character in one file.
- **Independent:** not hurt either. That letter means the story doesn't depend on other stories, and this fix doesn't depend on the column or the other way around.
- **What it does weaken:** the story is about one thing, the customers list. The detail page fix isn't covered by the user story, so a grader could say it's a second, unrelated change.
- **How I handled it:** I named it in the rescope note and labeled its criterion, so it reads as deliberate. If you'd rather keep the story clean, it could be its own one-line bug issue.

**Things I based the criteria on, so you can defend them**
- **Empty cell:** the "-" comes from the dashboard's existing `PlaceholderCell`.
- **Many groups:** the "first 2 names, then +N more, with the rest in a tooltip" rule copies `SalesChannelsCell`, which does this for products.
- **Search, filters and pagination:** asking for `+groups` adds to the default fields rather than replacing them (`field-parser.ts:47-55`). So the change shouldn't affect the existing columns, search, filters or paging.
- **One choice is mine, not the team's:** I wrote the estimate as 2 points. Swap in whatever units the team used in planning poker.

**New title:** Show customer groups on the customers list

```markdown
> Rescoped by @angrapsas. The original ask (show how many customers are in each group on the customer groups list) already exists upstream. `packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/customer-groups/customer-group-list/components/customer-group-list-table/customer-group-list-table.tsx` requests `customers.id` on line 48 and renders the count in the Customers column on lines 140-145. It came in with upstream PR medusajs/medusa#11106 in Feb 2025. I've rescoped this issue to a related gap in the same area that doesn't exist yet: the customers list doesn't show which groups each customer belongs to. I also folded in a small inconsistency on the group detail page (criterion 7).

## User Story
As a store manager, I want to see which groups each customer belongs to on the customers list so that I can check group membership for many customers at once without opening each customer's page.

## User Scenario
A store manager is getting ready for a wholesale promotion and wants to confirm that the right customers are in the "Wholesale" group. Today the customers list only shows email, name, account status and date, so they have to open each customer to see their groups. With this change they open Customers, scan the new Groups column, and spot two customers who are missing from "Wholesale" without leaving the list. They also filter by the "VIP" group and can see at a glance which VIP customers are also in other groups.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The customers list page (`/app/customers`) has a "Groups" column.
2. A customer in one or two groups shows those group names separated by a comma (for example "VIP, Wholesale").
3. A customer in three or more groups shows the first two names followed by "+N more", where N is the number of remaining groups. Hovering "+N more" shows a tooltip listing the remaining group names. This matches how the products list shows sales channels.
4. A customer who is in no groups shows "-" in the Groups column, the same placeholder the dashboard uses for other empty cells.
5. Existing search, filters, sorting and pagination on the customers list return the same rows as before this change. For example, filtering by a group still shows only that group's members, and moving to page 2 shows the next 20 customers, each with their groups filled in.
6. The customers table on the group detail page and the table in the "Add customers" form do not get a Groups column (see Design).
7. Related fix: on the group detail page, a group with no customers shows "0" in the Customers field instead of "-", matching the 0 shown for the same group on the customer groups list.

## Out of Scope
- Sorting the customers list by group.
- Adding, removing or editing a customer's groups from the customers list. This is already done from the customer or group detail pages.
- Changes to the groups filter itself, including the negation operators being added upstream in medusajs/medusa#16881.
- Linking each group name to its group detail page.
- Backend or API changes. `GET /admin/customers` already allows `groups` in `fields`.

## Open Questions
- Should the "Add customers" form also show a Groups column? It already fetches each customer's groups, so it would be cheap, but it isn't needed for this story.
- Is two names before "+N more" right for this column, or do group names tend to be long enough that one is better?

## Design
- Decision: I'll add the Groups column only to the customer list's own columns in `customer-list-table.tsx`, not to the shared `useCustomerTableColumns` hook.
- Alternatives considered: (1) add it to `useCustomerTableColumns`, which puts it in all three tables that use the hook (customers list, group detail customers table, Add customers form); (2) add it to the hook behind an option such as `useCustomerTableColumns({ includeGroups: true })`, similar to how `useCustomerTableFilters` takes an `exclude` list.
- Rationale: The group detail table is already scoped to a single group, so a groups column there would mostly repeat that group's name, and only the customers list needs it for this story.
- Consequences: The change stays in the customer list plus one new cell component and doesn't change the other two tables or their tests, but if another table needs the column later someone will have to move it into the shared hook.

Estimate: small (2 points)

export const POST = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<HttpTypes.AdminImportProductRequest>,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminImportProductResponse>
) => {
  const input = req.file as Express.Multer.File

  if (!input) {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
      "No file was uploaded for importing"
    )
  }

  const { result, transaction } = await importProductsWorkflow(req.scope).run({
    input: {
      filename: input.originalname,
      fileContent: input.buffer.toString("utf-8"),
    },
  })

  res
    .status(202)
    .json({ transaction_id: transaction.transactionId, summary: result })
}

export const importProductsAsChunksWorkflow = createWorkflow(
  importProductsAsChunksWorkflowId,
  (
    input: WorkflowData<{ fileKey: string; filename: string }>
  ): WorkflowResponse<WorkflowTypes.ProductWorkflow.ImportProductsSummary> => {
    const batchRequest = normalizeCsvToChunksStep(input.fileKey)

    waitConfirmationProductImportStep()

          channel: "feed",

          data: {
            title: "Product import",
            description: `Failed to import products from file ${data.input.filename}`,
          },
        },
      ]
    })

    notifyOnFailureStep(failureNotification)
    processImportChunksStep(batchRequest)

    const notifications = transform({ input }, (data) => {
      return [
        {
          // We don't need the recipient here for now, but if we want to push feed notifications to a specific user we could add it.
          to: "",
          channel: "feed",
          template: "admin-ui",
          data: {
            title: "Product import",
            description: `Product import of file ${data.input.filename} completed successfully!`,
          },
        },
      ]
    })

    sendNotificationsStep(notifications)
    return new WorkflowResponse(batchRequest.summary)
  }
)

import { Modules } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { createStep, StepResponse } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
import { batchProductsWorkflow } from "../workflows/batch-products"

export const processImportChunksStepId = "process-import-chunks"

/**
 * This step parses a CSV file holding products to import, returning the products as
 * objects that can be imported.
 *
 * @example
 * const data = parseProductCsvStep("products.csv")
 */
export const processImportChunksStep = createStep(
  {
    name: processImportChunksStepId,
    async: true,
  },
  async (input: { chunks: { id: string }[] }, { container }) => {
    const file = container.resolve(Modules.FILE)

    try {
      for (let chunk of input.chunks) {
        const contents = await file.getAsBuffer(chunk.id)
        let products = JSON.parse(contents.toString("utf-8"))
        await batchProductsWorkflow(container).run({
          input: products,
        })
        products = undefined
      }
    } finally {
      /**
       * Delete chunks regardless of the import status
       */
      await file.deleteFiles(input.chunks.map((chunk) => chunk.id))
    }

    return new StepResponse({ completed: true })
  }
)

/**
 * Parses different patterns to extract variant price iso
 * and the region name. The iso is converted to lowercase
 */
function parseVariantPriceColumn(columnName: string, rowNumber: number) {
  const normalizedValue = columnName
  const potentialRegion = /\[(.*)\]/g.exec(normalizedValue)?.[1]
  const iso = normalizedValue.split(" ").pop()

  if (!iso) {
    throw createError(
      rowNumber,

    )

import { model } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import CustomerAddress from "./address"
import CustomerGroup from "./customer-group"
import CustomerGroupCustomer from "./customer-group-customer"

const Customer = model
  .define("Customer", {
    id: model.id({ prefix: "cus" }).primaryKey(),
    company_name: model.text().searchable().nullable(),
    first_name: model.text().searchable().nullable(),
    last_name: model.text().searchable().nullable(),
    email: model.text().searchable().nullable(),
    phone: model.text().searchable().nullable(),
    has_account: model.boolean().default(false),
    metadata: model.json().nullable(),
    created_by: model.text().nullable(),
    groups: model.manyToMany(() => CustomerGroup, {
      mappedBy: "customers",
      pivotEntity: () => CustomerGroupCustomer,
    }),
    addresses: model.hasMany(() => CustomerAddress, {
      mappedBy: "customer",
    }),
  })
  .cascades({
    delete: ["addresses"],
    detach: ["groups"],
  })
  .indexes([
    {
      on: ["email", "has_account"],
      unique: true,
      where: "deleted_at IS NULL",
    },
  ])

export default Customer
-- service email checks

```text
import { MedusaError, Modules } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { createStep } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
import { CreateCustomerAccountWorkflowInput } from "../workflows"

export const validateCustomerAccountCreationStepId =
  "validate-customer-account-creation"

/**
 * This step validates the input data for creating a customer account.
 * The step throws an error if:
 * 
 * - The email is missing
 * - A customer with the email already exists and has an account
 * - A guest customer with the email already exists
 * 
 * @example
 * const data = validateCustomerAccountCreation({
 *   authIdentityId: "au_1234",
 *   customerData: {
 *     first_name: "John",
 *     last_name: "Doe",
 *     email: "john.doe@example.com",
 *   }
 * })
 */
export const validateCustomerAccountCreation = createStep(
  validateCustomerAccountCreationStepId,
  async (input: CreateCustomerAccountWorkflowInput, { container }) => {
    const customerService = container.resolve(Modules.CUSTOMER)

    const { email } = input.customerData

    if (!email) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
        "Email is required to create a customer"
      )
    }

    // Check if customer with email already exists
    const existingCustomers = await customerService.listCustomers({ email })

    if (existingCustomers?.length) {
      const hasExistingAccount = existingCustomers.some(
        (customer) => customer.has_account
      )

      if (hasExistingAccount && input.authIdentityId) {
        throw new MedusaError(
          MedusaError.Types.DUPLICATE_ERROR,
          "Customer with this email already has an account"
        )
      }

      if (!hasExistingAccount && !input.authIdentityId) {
        throw new MedusaError(
          MedusaError.Types.DUPLICATE_ERROR,
          "Guest customer with this email already exists"
        )
      }
    }
  }
)

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding Medusa v2 and CSV import functionality for customers:

## Current Status

Store managers migrating from another platform or processing large volumes of offline orders currently have no way to import multiple customers at once into Medusa, as each customer must be created individually through the admin UI. 

A feature request exists to allow uploading a CSV file containing customer data and bulk-creating customers from it in a single operation, but this appears to be an open feature request rather than an existing plugin.

## What Medusa v2 Currently Supports

While customer CSV import is not available, Medusa v2 does have CSV import capabilities for other entities:

- **Products**: Medusa v2.8.5 includes an overhauled bulk import process for products to make it more performant with strict validations
- **Prices**: Price list imports are also supported via CSV

To my knowledge, there is no existing official plugin specifically for importing customers via CSV in Medusa v2. If you need this functionality, you may need to either develop a custom plugin or explore third-party solutions.

I've finished the investigation and haven't drafted anything yet. The short version: customer import doesn't exist anywhere upstream, but the product import works differently from what #40 assumes in three ways.

## 1. Upstream: no existing customer import

- **GitHub:** I searched upstream issues and PRs for "customer import csv", "import customers", "customers csv", "bulk create customers" and "customer import". Nothing relevant came back.
- **Plugins:** web searches found no official or community plugin for importing customers in v2. The only exact match was our own #40.
- **One thing that looks like a match but isn't:** the [Customer Module marketing page](https://medusajs.com/customer-module) says you can "make bulk customer imports and exports." This repo has no customer import or export routes, workflows or SDK methods, so that claim most likely refers to v1's batch jobs. It's worth one sentence in the issue so a reviewer doesn't flag it.

## 2. How product import actually works

**Dashboard** (`packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/products/product-import/`)
- `product-import.tsx` is a modal. It has a file picker (`components/upload-import.tsx`) and a template download, which is a fixed CSV string in `helpers/import-template.ts`.
- After you pick a file, it calls `useImportProducts` and shows `components/import-summary.tsx`, which displays the counts of products to create and to update.
- Clicking Import calls `useConfirmImportProducts`, shows an "import started" toast, and closes the modal.

**SDK** (`packages/core/js-sdk/src/admin/product.ts:84`)
- `createImport` first uploads the file through `admin/uploads/presigned-urls`.
- It then sends only the uploaded file's key to the import route.

**Backend**
1. `POST /admin/products/imports` (`packages/medusa/src/api/admin/products/imports/route.ts`) runs `importProductsAsChunksWorkflow` and immediately returns `202` with a `transaction_id` and the summary.
2. The workflow (`packages/core/core-flows/src/product/workflows/import-products-as-chunks.ts:91`) parses and checks the CSV, then splits it into chunk files (`normalizeCsvToChunksStep`).
3. It then pauses at `waitConfirmationProductImportStep`. This step runs in the background and times out after 1 hour (`steps/wait-confirmation-product-import.ts`).
4. `POST /admin/products/imports/:transaction_id/confirm` resumes it.
5. `processImportChunksStep` then runs `batchProductsWorkflow` once per chunk in the background, and a notification is sent to the admin's activity feed.
6. `POST /admin/products/import` (singular) is the deprecated older version.

**Answer: it's upload, then confirm, then a background run.** The spec's out-of-scope line that says the import "completes synchronously within the request" is the part that's wrong.

**Two ways it differs from what #40 promises:**
- **It reports only the first bad row.** `createError` in `packages/core/utils/src/product/csv-normalizer.ts:38` throws `Row N: message` and stops there. Criterion 4 asks for every failing row.
- **It isn't all-or-nothing.** `processImportChunksStep` (`steps/process-import-chunks.ts`) has no undo step. If chunk 3 fails, chunks 1 and 2 stay saved. Criterion 3 promises "if any row is invalid the entire import is rejected and no customers are created." Copying the product pattern exactly wouldn't meet that.

**File size limit:** the dashboard's `FileUpload` defaults to `__MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE__ ?? 1MB` (`components/common/file-upload/file-upload.tsx:26`). That comes from the admin `maxUploadFileSize` setting (`admin-bundler/src/utils/config.ts:57`), and product import doesn't override it. A customer row is roughly 60 to 100 bytes, so 1MB is around 10,000 customers. That's enough to answer the open question rather than leave it open.

## 3. What creating a customer requires

- **Email is required by the dashboard but not the API.** The dashboard form requires a valid email (`routes/customers/customer-create/components/create-customer-form/create-customer-form.tsx:16`). The API makes it optional (`packages/medusa/src/api/admin/customers/validators.ts:53`). So the import requiring email matches the dashboard, not the API.
- **Uniqueness:** there's a unique index on `(email, has_account)` that ignores deleted customers (`packages/modules/customer/src/models/customer.ts:29-35`). Admin-created customers get `has_account: false` by default.

**What "email already exists" should mean for an import:**
- **It conflicts** when a non-deleted customer has the same email and `has_account = false`. That's a guest, or another admin-created customer.
- **It doesn't conflict** when a registered customer (`has_account = true`) has the same email. The database allows both, and the single-customer create route allows it too.
- **Importing a guest doesn't block that person from registering later.** `validate-customer-account-creation.ts` allows creating an account when only a guest with that email exists.

**Two more things the spec needs to decide:**
- **Uppercase and lowercase.** Nothing in the customer module, routes or workflows converts emails to lowercase. To the database, `Jo@x.com` and `jo@x.com` are different customers.
- **Row numbers in duplicate errors.** If the database catches a duplicate, the error is `Customer with email: x, has_account: false, already exists.` (`packages/core/utils/src/dal/mikro-orm/db-error-mapper.ts:39`). It names only the first conflict and gives no row number. Getting row-numbered errors means the import has to look up existing emails itself before creating anything.

## 4. A bulk create workflow already exists

- `createCustomersWorkflow` (`packages/core/core-flows/src/customer/workflows/create-customers.ts:57`) takes an array. `POST /admin/customers` already uses it with a one-item array (`packages/medusa/src/api/admin/customers/route.ts:48`).
- Its step (`steps/create-customers.ts:31`) makes a single `service.createCustomers(data)` call. That service method runs inside one database transaction (`createCustomers_`, `customer-module.ts:122`), and the step's undo deletes the customers it created.
- **Reusing it in one call gives you all-or-nothing for free,** which product import doesn't have. It also fires the `customer.created` events and the `customersCreated` hook.

## 5. PR #35 has no export columns to match

- It changes only the dashboard: a `CustomerExport` component and a `useExportCustomers` hook that calls `sdk.admin.customer.export(query)`.
- The PR description itself says that SDK method doesn't exist, and there's no backend route or workflow behind it. So no export column list exists yet.
- **What that means for #40:** this spec will define the column names first, and #35 should match them later. Product import uses an entity prefix (`Product Id`, `Product Title`), so the equivalent would be `Customer Email`, `Customer First Name`, and so on.
- **Unrelated:** #35 also includes a `vite.config.mts` change for the blank screen. Worth a mention when you review it.

## Key files to read yourself
1. `packages/core/core-flows/src/product/workflows/import-products-as-chunks.ts`: the whole flow in about 50 lines.
2. `packages/core/core-flows/src/product/steps/process-import-chunks.ts`: shows why product import isn't all-or-nothing.
3. `packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/products/product-import/product-import.tsx`: the dashboard side.
4. `packages/core/core-flows/src/customer/workflows/create-customers.ts` and `steps/create-customers.ts`: the bulk create you'd reuse.
5. `packages/modules/customer/src/models/customer.ts:29-35`: the uniqueness rule.

## Decisions I need from you before drafting
1. **Flow:** copy the product pattern (upload, summary, confirm, background run), or use one simpler request that checks and creates everything at once? This is the Design section, and I'll lay out both sides there either way.
2. **Errors:** report every failing row (needs your own checking pass), or stop at the first one like product import does? Criterion 4 currently says every row.
3. **Email case:** treat `Jo@x.com` and `jo@x.com` as duplicates? The database doesn't, so if you say yes, the import needs to do its own comparison.

Sources:
- [Customer Module, Medusa.js](https://medusajs.com/customer-module)
- [Import Products in Medusa Admin](https://docs.medusajs.com/user-guide/products/import)
- [medusajs/medusa v2.8.5 release](https://newreleases.io/project/github/medusajs/medusa/release/v2.8.5)
- [CSCI-435-SE/medusa #40](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/medusa/issues/40)

1	## User Story
2	As a store manager, I want to upload a CSV file to import multiple customers at once so that I can migrate customer data without manually entering each one individually.
3	
4	## User Scenario
5	A user is migrating their store to Medusa from another platform and has 500 existing customers to recreate. They export their customers from the old platform, reformat the data to match Medusa's CSV template, and upload the file from the Customer list page. Medusa validates the file and surfaces a clear error message identifying two rows with duplicate email addresses. They fix the CSV and re-upload. All 500 customers are created successfully and appear in the Customer list.
6	
7	## Acceptance Criteria
8	1. An "Import Customers" action is available on the Customer list page, consistent in placement and interaction pattern with the existing product CSV import.
9	2. A downloadable CSV template is provided, covering all fields available when creating a customer: email (required), first name, last name, company, and phone (all optional).
10	3. The uploaded CSV is validated before any customers are created; if any row is invalid the entire import is rejected and no customers are created.
11	4. Validation feedback identifies each failing row by row number and describes the specific error (e.g. missing email, invalid email format, duplicate email within the file, email already exists in Medusa).
12	5. On successful import, all customers in the CSV are created in a single operation and immediately appear in the Customer list.
13	6. The import UI follows the same component patterns as the existing product CSV import.
14	7. Required fields that are empty/blank throw an error; optional fields that are blank are accepted.
15	
16	## Out of Scope
17	- Customer group assignment. This is not part of the create customer fields and is out of scope for this story.
18	- Updating or deduplicating customers that already exist in Medusa (all imports should be new customers).
19	- Scheduling or deferring import jobs. The operation completes synchronously within the request.
20	- Exporting existing customers to CSV.
21	
22	## Open Questions
23	- Is there a maximum file size or row count limit that should be enforced?
24

```text
## User Story
As a store manager, I want to upload a CSV file to import multiple customers at once so that I can migrate customer data without manually entering each one individually.

## User Scenario
A user is migrating their store to Medusa from another platform and has 500 existing customers to recreate. They export their customers from the old platform, reformat the data to match Medusa's CSV template, and upload the file from the Customer list page. Medusa validates the file and surfaces a clear error message identifying two rows with duplicate email addresses. They fix the CSV and re-upload. All 500 customers are created successfully and appear in the Customer list.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. An "Import Customers" action is available on the Customer list page, consistent in placement and modal layout with the existing product CSV import.
2. A downloadable CSV template is provided, covering all fields available when creating a customer: email (required), first name, last name, company, and phone (all optional).
3. The uploaded CSV is validated before any customers are created; if any row is invalid the entire import is rejected and no customers are created.
4. Validation feedback identifies each failing row by row number and describes the specific error (e.g. missing email, invalid email format, duplicate email within the file, email already exists in Medusa). "Email already exists in Medusa" means a customer that has not been deleted has the same email and `has_account` set to false. A registered customer (`has_account` true) with the same email does not count as a duplicate.
5. On successful import, all customers in the CSV are created in a single operation and immediately appear in the Customer list.
6. The import UI follows the same placement and modal layout as the existing product CSV import.
7. Required fields that are empty/blank throw an error; optional fields that are blank are accepted.

## Out of Scope
- Customer group assignment. This is not part of the create customer fields and is out of scope for this story.
- Updating or deduplicating customers that already exist in Medusa (all imports should be new customers).
- Scheduling or deferring import jobs. The operation completes synchronously within the request.
- Exporting existing customers to CSV.
- Case insensitive email matching. Duplicate checks against existing customers are exact, so `Jo@example.com` and `jo@example.com` are treated as different emails, which matches how Medusa stores them today.

## Open Questions
- Is there a maximum file size or row count limit that should be enforced?
  - Answer: Yes, the import uses the dashboard's existing upload limit, which defaults to 1MB (`maxUploadFileSize` in the admin config). A customer row is roughly 60 to 100 bytes, so that is about 10,000 customers per file. No separate row limit is added.

## Design
- Decision: I'll implement the import as one request that parses the CSV, checks every row, and creates all customers with a single `createCustomersWorkflow` call, instead of copying the product import's upload, confirm and background flow.
- Alternatives considered: (1) copy the product import flow (`importProductsAsChunksWorkflow`), which uploads the file, shows a summary, waits for the user to confirm, then creates records in chunks in the background; (2) have the dashboard parse the CSV and call the existing `POST /admin/customers` route once per row.
- Rationale: A 1MB file is about 10,000 customers, which is small enough for one request, and a single `createCustomersWorkflow` call runs in one database transaction, which is what guarantees criterion 3, while the product flow saves each chunk separately and the per-row option can leave some customers created when a later row fails.
- Consequences: The import is simpler to build and test and is all or nothing, but there is no summary and confirm step before customers are created, and a much larger upload limit would make the request slow enough that the background approach would be worth revisiting.

Estimate: medium (5 points)
```

```markdown
> Rescoped by @angrapsas. The original ask (show how many customers are in each group on the customer groups list) already exists upstream. `packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/customer-groups/customer-group-list/components/customer-group-list-table/customer-group-list-table.tsx` requests `customers.id` on line 48 and renders the count in the Customers column on lines 140-145. It came in with upstream PR medusajs/medusa#11106 in Feb 2025. I've rescoped this issue to a related gap in the same area that doesn't exist yet: the customers list doesn't show which groups each customer belongs to. I also folded in a small inconsistency on the group detail page (criterion 7).

## User Story
As a store manager, I want to see which groups each customer belongs to on the customers list so that I can check group membership for many customers at once without opening each customer's page.

## User Scenario
A store manager is getting ready for a wholesale promotion and wants to confirm that the right customers are in the "Wholesale" group. Today the customers list only shows email, name, account status and date, so they have to open each customer to see their groups. With this change they open Customers, scan the new Groups column, and spot two customers who are missing from "Wholesale" without leaving the list. They also filter by the "VIP" group and can see at a glance which VIP customers are also in other groups.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The customers list page (`/app/customers`) has a "Groups" column.
2. A customer in one or two groups shows those group names separated by a comma (for example "VIP, Wholesale").
3. A customer in three or more groups shows the first two names followed by "+N more", where N is the number of remaining groups. Hovering "+N more" shows a tooltip listing the remaining group names. This matches how the products list shows sales channels.
4. A customer who is in no groups shows "-" in the Groups column, the same placeholder the dashboard uses for other empty cells.
5. Existing search, filters, sorting and pagination on the customers list return the same rows as before this change. For example, filtering by a group still shows only that group's members, and moving to page 2 shows the next 20 customers, each with their groups filled in.
6. The customers table on the group detail page and the table in the "Add customers" form do not get a Groups column (see Design).
7. Related fix: on the group detail page, a group with no customers shows "0" in the Customers field instead of "-", matching the 0 shown for the same group on the customer groups list.

## Out of Scope
- Sorting the customers list by group.
- Adding, removing or editing a customer's groups from the customers list. This is already done from the customer or group detail pages.
- Changes to the groups filter itself, including the negation operators being added upstream in medusajs/medusa#16881.
- Linking each group name to its group detail page.
- Backend or API changes. `GET /admin/customers` already allows `groups` in `fields`.

## Open Questions
- Should the "Add customers" form also show a Groups column? It already fetches each customer's groups, so it would be cheap, but it isn't needed for this story.
- Is two names before "+N more" right for this column, or do group names tend to be long enough that one is better?

## Design
- Decision: I'll add the Groups column only to the customer list's own columns in `customer-list-table.tsx`, not to the shared `useCustomerTableColumns` hook.
- Alternatives considered: (1) add it to `useCustomerTableColumns`, which puts it in all three tables that use the hook (customers list, group detail customers table, Add customers form); (2) add it to the hook behind an option such as `useCustomerTableColumns({ includeGroups: true })`, similar to how `useCustomerTableFilters` takes an `exclude` list.
- Rationale: The group detail table is already scoped to a single group, so a groups column there would mostly repeat that group's name, and only the customers list needs it for this story.
- Consequences: The change stays in the customer list plus one new cell component and doesn't change the other two tables or their tests, but if another table needs the column later someone will have to move it into the shared hook.

Estimate: small (2 points)

```

-- inventory item model
import { model } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import InventoryLevel from "./inventory-level"
import ReservationItem from "./reservation-item"

const InventoryItem = model
  .define("InventoryItem", {
    id: model.id({ prefix: "iitem" }).primaryKey(),
    sku: model.text().searchable().nullable(),
    origin_country: model.text().nullable(),
    hs_code: model.text().searchable().nullable(),
    mid_code: model.text().searchable().nullable(),
    material: model.text().nullable(),
    weight: model.number().nullable(),
    length: model.number().nullable(),
    height: model.number().nullable(),
    width: model.number().nullable(),
    requires_shipping: model.boolean().default(true),
    description: model.text().searchable().nullable(),
    title: model.text().searchable().nullable(),
    thumbnail: model.text().nullable(),
    metadata: model.json().nullable(),
    location_levels: model.hasMany(() => InventoryLevel, {
      mappedBy: "inventory_item",
    }),
    reservation_items: model.hasMany(() => ReservationItem, {
      mappedBy: "inventory_item",
    }),
    reserved_quantity: model.number().computed(),
    stocked_quantity: model.number().computed(),
  })
  .cascades({
    delete: ["location_levels", "reservation_items"],
  })
  .indexes([
    {
      name: "IDX_inventory_item_sku",
      on: ["sku"],
      unique: true,
      where: "deleted_at IS NULL",
    },
  ])

export default InventoryItem
-- inventory level model
import { model } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import InventoryItem from "./inventory-item"

const InventoryLevel = model
  .define("InventoryLevel", {
    id: model.id({ prefix: "ilev" }).primaryKey(),
    location_id: model.text(),
    stocked_quantity: model.bigNumber().default(0),
    reserved_quantity: model.bigNumber().default(0),
    incoming_quantity: model.bigNumber().default(0),
    metadata: model.json().nullable(),
    inventory_item: model.belongsTo(() => InventoryItem, {
      mappedBy: "location_levels",
    }),
    available_quantity: model.bigNumber().computed(),
  })
  .indexes([
    {
      name: "IDX_inventory_level_inventory_item_id",
      on: ["inventory_item_id"],
      where: "deleted_at IS NULL",
    },
    {
      name: "IDX_inventory_level_location_id",
      on: ["location_id"],
      where: "deleted_at IS NULL",
    },
    {
      name: "IDX_inventory_level_location_id_inventory_item_id",
      on: ["inventory_item_id", "location_id"],
      unique: true,
      where: "deleted_at IS NULL",
    },
  ])

export default InventoryLevel

Based on the search results, here's what I found about importing inventory items via CSV in Medusa Admin:

## Product Import Overview

You can import products into Medusa using a CSV file when migrating from another commerce platform or from Medusa v1. When you import the CSV file, Medusa will either create or update products based on the CSV file you upload.

## CSV File Format

Each row in the CSV file represents a product variant to create or update. So, if a product has multiple variants, each variant will have its own row in the CSV file.

In the import form, you can download a template CSV file to see the format required for the import.

## Inventory-Related Columns

The CSV format includes several inventory management fields:
- **Variant Manage Inventory** - Whether Medusa manages the variant's inventory. Can be true or false.
- **Variant Allow Backorder** - Whether the variant allows backorders. Can be true or false.

## Import Process

To import products, go to the Products page, click on the Import button in the main section's header, and either drag-and-drop the file to the upload area or click on the area to open a file picker.

## Known Issues

It's worth noting that there have been some reported issues with inventory quantity imports. The column "Variant Inventory Quantity" is no longer present in Medusa v2, which means all products are imported with zero stock.

export const createInventoryItemsWorkflow = createWorkflow(
  createInventoryItemsWorkflowId,
  (input: WorkflowData<CreateInventoryItemsWorkflowInput>) => {
    const { locationLevelMap, inventoryItems } = transform(
      input,
      buildLocationLevelMapAndItemData
    )
    const items = createInventoryItemsStep(inventoryItems)

    const inventoryLevelsInput = transform(
      { items, locationLevelMap },
      buildInventoryLevelsInput
    )

    createInventoryLevelsWorkflow.runAsStep(inventoryLevelsInput)

    const itemIdEvents = transform({ items }, ({ items }) => {
      return items.map((item) => ({ id: item.id }))
    })

    emitEventStep({
      eventName: InventoryItemWorkflowEvents.CREATED,
      data: itemIdEvents,
    })

    return new WorkflowResponse(items)
  }
)

```text
import {
  arrayDifference,
  ContainerRegistrationKeys,
  MedusaError,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"

import type { InventoryTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { createStep } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"

/**
 * The data to validate the inventory levels.
 */
export type ValidateInventoryLocationsStepInput =
  InventoryTypes.CreateInventoryLevelInput[]

export const validateInventoryLocationsStepId = "validate-inventory-levels-step"
/**
 * This step ensures that the inventory levels exist for each
 * specified pair of inventory item and location. If not,
 * the step will throw an error.
 */
export const validateInventoryLocationsStep = createStep(
  validateInventoryLocationsStepId,
  async (data: ValidateInventoryLocationsStepInput, { container }) => {
    const remoteQuery = container.resolve(
      ContainerRegistrationKeys.REMOTE_QUERY
    )

    const stockLocations = await remoteQuery({
      entryPoint: "stock_location",
      variables: {
        id: data.map((d) => d.location_id),
      },
      fields: ["id"],
    })

    const diff = arrayDifference(
      data.map((d) => d.location_id),
      stockLocations.map((l) => l.id)
    )
    if (diff.length > 0) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
        `Stock locations with ids: ${diff.join(", ")} was not found`
      )
    }
  }
)

```text
1	## User Story
2	As a store manager, I want to upload a CSV file to import multiple inventory items at once so that I can migrate inventory data without manually entering each one individually.
3	
4	## User Scenario
5	A user is migrating their store to Medusa from another platform and has 300 existing inventory items to recreate. They export their inventory from the old platform, reformat the data to match Medusa's CSV template, and upload the file from the Inventory list page. Medusa validates the file and surfaces a clear error message identifying four rows with duplicate SKUs. They fix the CSV and re-upload. All 300 inventory items are created successfully and appear in the Inventory list.
6	
7	## Acceptance Criteria
8	1. An "Import Inventory" action is available on the Inventory list page, consistent in placement and interaction pattern with the existing product CSV import.
9	2. A downloadable CSV template is provided covering all fields available when creating an inventory item:
10	    - Required: Title, SKU, Requires Shipping, In Stock, Location
11	    - Optional: Description, Width, Length, Height, Weight, MID Code, HS Code, Country of Origin, Material
12	3. The uploaded CSV is validated before any inventory items are created; if any row is invalid the entire import is rejected and no items are created.
13	4. Validation feedback identifies each failing row by row number and describes the specific error (e.g. missing required field, duplicate SKU within the file, SKU already exists in Medusa, invalid value for Requires Shipping).
14	5. On successful import, all inventory items in the CSV are created in a single operation and immediately appear in the Inventory list assigned to the European Warehouse location.
15	6. The import UI follows the same component patterns as the existing product CSV import.
16	7. Required fields that are empty/blank throw an error; optional fields that are blank are accepted.
17	
18	## Out of Scope
19	- Updating or deduplicating inventory items that already exist in Medusa (all imports should be new inventory items).
20	- Scheduling or deferring import jobs. The operation completes synchronously within the request.
21	- Exporting existing inventory to CSV.
22	
23	## Open Questions
24	- Is there a maximum file size or row count limit that should be enforced?
25	- Should "In Stock" quantities below zero be rejected as invalid, or are negative values permitted?
26	- Can there be multiple locations?
27
```
</details></tool-use>
